hints.title: Stone Jump State
hints.text: To determine if the frog can reach a stone, track the set of previous jump distances that landed on that stone.

hints.title: Valid Consecutive Transitions
hints.text: If a stone was reached with jump distance k, the next jump can be k minus 1, k, or k plus 1, provided the new jump distance is strictly positive.

hints.title: Forward Reachability Propagation
hints.text: Initialize a table mapping each stone position to a set of possible jump lengths. Start with 0 at stone 0. For each stone in increasing order, iterate over its jump sizes, calculate candidate landing stones, and add the jump distance to their sets.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: number of stones in list
complexity.notes: Maximum jumps per stone is bounded by N, giving O(N^2) total states.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unmemoized branch exploration checks exponential numbers of redundant jump paths.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Hash table mapping stone coordinate to jump set avoids sparse array overhead.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognize state (position, jump) and propagate reachability forward efficiently.
